subject: Post-signature implementation: phased glidepath, canary windows, and rollback plan
messages_1_subject: Signed — Post-signature: Implementation MAP & kickoff windows
messages_1_body:
Hi Neha,

Great to confirm the contract executed this morning — thank you. Our procurement team said the signed SOW and order are in place. We want to align on a practical implementation plan and MAP that covers rollout, canary, migration, and training. Can you and your team propose a phased glidepath and target dates for: non-prod migration, canary start, production ramp, and training for our ops and support teams?

Key constraints on our side:
- Peak traffic retention window: limited two-week canary in January 2028 (we prefer beginning Jan 10).
- Data residency: all PII must remain in our US region (no cross-region fallbacks).
- Maintenance blackout: Dec 24–Jan 2 (no major switches).

We'd like an initial MAP and the evaluation criteria (SLOs/metrics) to review by Friday so we can coordinate internal resources. I attached our desired go-live blackout windows and a short checklist from our infra team.

Thanks — Sara

--
Sara Liu
Director, Platform Engineering
Aurigadata, Inc.
sara.liu@aurigadata.com
(415) 555-0198

Attachments referenced: aurigadata-infra-constraints.pdf (see infra notes)
messages_2_subject: Re: Signed — Post-signature: Implementation MAP & kickoff windows
messages_2_body:
Sara — congrats and thanks for the clarity. Attached is our first-pass MAP (Aurigadata-MAP-v1.0.xlsx) and a Redwood canary checklist (aurigadata-canary-checklist.pdf). High level proposal: 

1) Non-prod migration (dry-run): week of Dec 13 — goal: smoke tests, KV/cache sizing, and end-to-end latency baselining.
2) Training: Dec 15–19 (2-hour sessions per team; ops, support, security). Training schedule attached (training-rollout-schedule.csv).
3) Canary window (staged): two-stage canary in Jan —
   - Canary A (subset traffic, 10%): Jan 10–Jan 17 — validate latency SLOs and error budget usage
   - Canary B (increased traffic, 40%): Jan 18–Jan 24 — monitor tail latency and quality regressions with eval sets
4) Production ramp: Jan 25–Feb 7 — gradual increase with automatic fallback to the most recent stable model when error or latency thresholds breach.

Rollback criteria (short):
- Sustained 5xx rate > 0.5% over 10m OR
- p99 latency above 2.5s for longer than 15m OR
- Quality A/B regression > 3% on core intent eval (per test set)

Owners: Redwood will own runtime deploy and canary monitoring (Rishi primary), Marissa will manage customer ops coordination and cutover windows, Neha will coordinate MAP updates and exec communications, Stephanie will own training delivery and runbooks.

I put links to the runbook and an initial DocuSign reference in the related links. If these windows look OK I can firm up time slots for training and send calendar invites.

messages_3_subject: Re: Post-signature implementation: phased glidepath, canary windows, and rollback plan
messages_3_body:
Thanks — this is a solid first pass. A few practical notes from the deployment side: 

- Canary cadence: we usually recommend a 10-day observation period per canary stage for customer traffic patterns that vary by region — your Jan 10 start looks fine but let's keep Jan 10–21 as the combined observation window to give us breathing room.
- Traffic routing: we'll implement traffic-slicing at the edge with header-based routing so you can target specific clients for Canary A. Need confirmation if you can provide a stable identifier in requests (customer_id header).
- Monitoring: add synthetic probes that exercise the top 5 intents in the eval set — these should run every 5m during canary. We'll wire alerts to your on-call and ours.

I've sketched a simple rollback playbook inside the canary checklist (pdf). Example quick rollback flow: disable new variant in routing -> promote previous model -> invalidate caches if cache-related errors observed -> monitor for 30m. We'll capture the runbook final in the shared Drive.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

messages_5_subject: Re: Post-signature implementation: phased glidepath, canary windows, and rollback plan
messages_5_body:
All — I can take point on the runtime deploy and the telemetry hooks. Quick operational notes and next steps: 

- Dec 20 dry-run: confirmed. We'll reserve a 4-hour slot (10:00–14:00 PT) for the migration smoke tests. Objectives: KV cache warm-up, latency profile capture (p50/p95/p99), and end-to-end auth checks.
- Synthetic probes: Marissa, attaching the probe spec to the runbook in Drive (see related links). We'll publish a curl-based probe and a python client example.
- Monitoring thresholds (formal):
   * 5xx rate alert: 0.5% over 10m -> page ops
   * p99 latency alert: 2.5s -> page infra
   * A/B quality regression: 3% absolute drop -> notify product + pause rollout

- Runbooks and contact matrix: Stephanie will lead training sessions and will post the final runbook in Drive by Dec 17.
- Jira: creating INFRA-4872 for the migration checklist and INFRA-4873 for canary monitoring alerts; links in related_links.

I'll follow up with a calendar invite for Dec 20 dry-run and separate invites for the training sessions.

Rishi
